one_line_summary: Design rule: use dinuclear [Zn2(CO2)2] units as 6-connected nodes linked by μ4-BDC2- and μ2-ATz- ligands

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use dinuclear [Zn2(CO2)2] units as 6-connected nodes linked by μ4-BDC2- and μ2-ATz- ligands → enables construction of a 3D 6-connected framework

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] change the synthesis solvent from hydrothermal water-based conditions to DMF solvothermal conditions in the HATz/H2BDC/Zn(NO3)2 system → framework dimensionality changes from a 2D layered Zn coordination polymer to a 3D Zn coordination polymer

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: hydrothermally synthesized complex 1 in the HATz/H2BDC/Zn(NO3)2 system vs DMF-solvothermally synthesized complex 2 in the HATz/H2BDC/Zn(NO3)2 system: winner=tie on framework_dimensionality

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: complex 1 vs complex 2: winner=tie on network_topology_and_node_type

notable_quotes: Compared with neutral HATz and H2BDC ligands, coordination to Zn(II) markedly enhances emission intensity and causes a clear red shift in both complexes.
Complex 1 is a 3-connected (6,3) honeycomb 2D layer, and hydrogen bonding between layers stacks it into a stable 3D supramolecular structure.
Both compounds are strongly luminescent at room temperature under 350 nm excitation, emitting at 451 nm for 1 and 466 nm for 2.
